Amy (Sales): Heads-up — BankX POC wants a Private/VPC deploy. Netops sent a list of asks around egress path, SNI proxy, and preserving client src IP. Can SE + NetOps weigh in?
Bob (SE): Quick context: customer plans to use our Private control plane via PrivateLink interface endpoints into their VPC and run runtime in their account behind TGW. They want SNI-preserving egress through their TLS-inspecting proxy and are asking if we can do mTLS to their edge.
Chen (NetOps): Primary asks: 1) Can we keep original client src IP when requests reach the runtime? 2) Exact ports/CIDRs to whitelist for control plane + runtime model pulls. 3) If we route via TGW + NAT GW, will client IP be SNAT'd?
Bob (SE): Short answers: PrivateLink -> control plane traffic stays inside VPC, but src IP preservation depends on the egress path. If traffic traverses a NAT GW it will be SNAT'd. Options: (a) put proxy in front that forwards original IP via X-Forwarded-For or PROXY protocol, (b) terminate TLS at the proxy and forward original client metadata. Our runtime can accept PROXY protocol v1 on the listener if you enable it in the config (we need the customer to allow NLB -> runtime with PROXY).
Chen (NetOps): Can you give the exact ports & IPs to hand to security? They need a checklist.
Bob (SE): Required egress bullets and notes: - TCP 443 to PrivateLink interface ENIs (control-plane) — allow from runtime subnets to the PrivateLink ENI(s). - TCP 443 to model artifact stores (S3) OR use VPC S3 endpoint to avoid internet egress. - UDP/TCP 53 for DNS to your resolver. - UDP 123 for NTP (optional but recommended). Example snippet for firewall team: ```egress_rules = [ { cidr = "10.5.0.0/16", port = "443", proto = "tcp", note = "PrivateLink ENI" }, { cidr = "0.0.0.0/0", port = "443", proto = "tcp", note = "model fetch via S3 (if no S3 endpoint)" } ]``` Recommend: keep egress to minimal set and use VPC endpoints for S3/ECR to avoid opening 0.0.0.0/0. If customer requires TLS inspection, they should configure the proxy to forward client identity (PROXY or XFF).
Chen (NetOps): What about TGW vs interface endpoint tradeoffs for preserving src IP?
Bob (SE): TGW with NAT = SNAT. Interface endpoints (PrivateLink) keep traffic on the AZ and preserve the original IP when hitting the ENI only for traffic staying in-VPC; however once you route through their proxy or other NATing appliance, the source can change. Architecture recommendation: place an inspection-proxy as a transparent forwarder that preserves client src via PROXY protocol to the runtime, or terminate+reestablish and send X-Forwarded-For. If BankX policy forbids forwarding headers, then real client IP cannot be recovered and you'll rely on proxy metadata for audit.
Chen (NetOps): They also asked about mTLS to our control plane. Can we support client cert auth?
Bob (SE): We support mutual TLS for control-plane connections in Private deployments; we can accept customer certs and integrate with their KMS for rotation. BYOK via HSM is supported in Private offering. For POC we can exchange temporary certs.
Sam (Security): Security items: we'll need SOC2 docs, encryption-at-rest/encryption-in-transit details, KMS integration docs, and an explicit list of external endpoints (CIDRs) the runtime will talk to. Also confirm whether runtime nodes can be run with no outbound internet (yes if customer supplies endpoints for all required services).
Amy (Sales): Pricing note for Sales: Private deployment = platform fee + infra. Dedicated reserved GPU pools are separate line item; for POC we can offer a limited-time waiver/discount — I'll attach a draft quote in the channel.
Chen (NetOps): Action items: 1) Sales (Amy) to share BankX VPC CIDR ranges and proxy ops contact. 2) NetOps to confirm whether they can accept PROXY protocol on their NLB/edge. 3) SE (Bob) to produce a 1-page architecture recommendation showing: "interface endpoints + proxy with PROXY protocol" vs "TGW + NAT" and the exact ports to whitelist. 4) Security (Sam) to list required artifacts.
Amy (Sales): I'll collate and loop in BankX tomorrow EOD. @deploy-bot please create a POC channel once we confirm dates.
deploy-bot: Created channel #poc-bankx-246999. Invitees: Amy (Sales), Bob (SE), Chen (NetOps), Sam (Security)
Amy (Sales): Thanks — looping legal for the cert exchange and procurement for a temporary Dedicated quote.
Bob (SE): I'll draft the 1-pager and post by EOD PST.
Chen (NetOps): I'll ping proxy ops and confirm PROXY protocol capability, ETA EOD PST.
Sam (Security): I'll assemble SOC2 + KMS notes and drop links here.
